_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. `trinity.graph` is a semio-NATIVE assembly scene whose pieces and connections live in a composed `s.stdio.semio.graph` child, so no oracle is registered and the evidence rests on the eight committed per-kind vectors plus the inverse law over the real committed Nakagin tower (see noOracleDecisions).

noOracleDecisions.rationale: No third party reads or writes `.jack.dsl.semio`, and no graph library could adjudicate this vocabulary either. `JackSnapshot` persists a `manifest`, a camera, a root node id and ONE composed `s.stdio.semio.graph` child handle whose `childId` is a content digest of the child — pieces and connections are never persisted inline — so what an applied mutation produces is a NEW handle and what a refused one produces is the same handle, an addressing scheme private to this repository. And the vocabulary is an ASSEMBLY vocabulary rather than a graph one: an edge endpoint is a `node@port` pair split by this plugin's own `port_node_id`, an edge that names an absent endpoint is the Fatal `mutation.invariant` rather than a missing target, and `change-data-property`/`remove-data-property` address an `EntityRef` because nodes and edges share one property-bag shape. Confidence comes instead from the eight committed, independently handcrafted specification vectors under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<slug>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/`, each already unit-tested inside the production crate, and from the inverse law as a metamorphic property. Those eight split evenly and deliberately: four are refusals at two severities, four are no-ops — renaming a piece to the name it already carries, moving it to the point it already occupies, setting a property to the value it already holds, removing a property an edge never had. All eight leave the document byte-identical, so the `(code, severity)` pair is the only thing that tells a refusal from a degenerate application; `mutate-jack-1` therefore requires that pair per vector and separately applies a real-effect payload of its own to the committed Nakagin tower, where the content-addressed handle supplies the observability the vectors cannot.
